findings.title: After a cancel, a frame write gives up after one 0.5 s unwritable select, leaving a half-written line and no `done`
findings.detail: In `_Frames._write_fd`, once `cancel` is set (stdin EOF or a signal), the first `select` that times out after 0.5 s sets `closed=True` and returns. A frame that was partly written in PIPE_BUF pieces stays on stdout as a truncated JSON line. Every later frame, including the `done` with `interrupted: true` that the spec says is sent "if it can", is then dropped, even though the coordinator is still reading. The process still exits 0, so the coordinator gets exit 0 with a broken last line and no `done`. That contradicts "gate-job never exits without one of the two frames unless stdout is closed".
findings.trigger: The coordinator cancels by closing stdin (or SIGTERM arrives) while a multi-MiB `gate` frame is being written, and the coordinator's read side pauses for more than 0.5 s, for example a full SSH channel window on a slow link.

findings.title: A pre-slot signal does not interrupt a wait on the repo flock
findings.detail: Before the slot stage the signal handler only records the signal unless the job is blocked reading stdin. `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX)` in `repo_lock` is retried after EINTR (PEP 475), so a job waiting for the repo lock ignores SIGTERM/SIGHUP until the holder releases it. The holder may be another job's slow fetch or a `git gc --prune=now` on a big cache, so the job can outlive the connection by minutes.
findings.trigger: Job A's checkout waits on `repos/<key>.lock` while gc prunes a large cache, and sshd or the coordinator sends SIGTERM/SIGHUP to job A.

findings.title: `nw worker have` turns a git failure into a traceback
findings.detail: `have()` calls `_set_have`, which uses `_git(..., check=True)`. A failing `update-ref` (disk full, an unwritable ref) raises `WorkerError`, but `worker_have` only catches `ValueError`. Over SSH the coordinator gets a Python traceback on stderr and exit 1, not a clean error.
findings.trigger: `update-ref refs/nw/have/<sha>` fails in the cache during `nw worker have --repo K <sha>`.

findings.title: `info.git_sha` can report an unrelated repository
findings.detail: `git -C <site-packages>/nightwright rev-parse HEAD` searches up the directory tree. In a `uv tool install` under a home directory that is itself a git repo (dotfiles), it reports that repo's HEAD as nightwright's `git_sha`.
findings.trigger: The worker user's home or one of its parent directories is a git work tree.
